verdict: Red 7/10 REJECT with a recommendation to kill the docket entirely; blue 8/10 PARTIALLY OVERTURNED, and the part it overturned is red's core disposition. This is the batch's clearest bench discordance. Both benches agree on the immediate answer - FLAT at $1.59, no position - so nothing is at risk today; what they disagree on is whether the name stays on the docket, and blue reduced or refuted every one of red's three FATAL findings. Red's genuine and undisputed contribution is a record defect: the court brief carried only the Q2 guide-cut press release and missed the SAME-DAY 2026-08-05 06:30 announcement that EVgo will deploy Tesla V4 Superchargers, which EVgo owns, with Tesla-nav routing and deployments starting fall 2026. The tape fell 12.7% WITH a marquee Tesla partnership in hand, which answers the 'what does the tape know' question - funding math dominates. Blue verified the deal and added the detail red's capex framing missed: Tesla OPERATES AND MAINTAINS, so ownership adds capex but the O&M split cuts opex. Blue then dismantled red's two kill findings. On dilution: red read Class A diluted shares going 70.99M to 141.72M over three years as evidence that management prints equity roughly 2x. Blue traced it - LS Power's Class B went 195.8M to 172.8M, with 23M units redeemed into Class A through the Up-C exchange, which is economically non-dilutive; total A+B economic units went 264.6M to 314.5M, about +19%, not 2x. Red's killer series is an accounting artifact. On funding: red counted $121.8M of unrestricted cash against H1 operating cash flow of -$41.85M and -$64.4M of capex and called the growth engine unfunded. Blue counted the build-specific facilities red omitted - $409M undrawn DOE plus $153.4M Voyager, so roughly $684M of total liquidity against about $106M of H1 cash use that was already ~80% debt-funded ($86.6M of draws). Rising leverage is the plan's design, not a discovery. On the hiring wave: the pre-flight detector fired (postings 6 in May, 10 in June, 42 in July, 20 in August-partial, 80 open reqs) and red called it FATAL to the cost-discipline fork, but blue found the only visible posting is 'Senior, Siting & Permitting' - development and build-side, not corporate G&A - so it defeats 'taper corroborated' without confirming G&A expansion. Blue's summary is that red attacked the correct axis (funding) but over-tagged, and that its cleanest genuine kill - a defective record plus no paying catalyst inside 90 days - needed no inflation. Blue also surfaced a bear datum red's own dilution digging should have found: LS Power monetized 23M units through the Dec-2024 secondary, so the controlling holder is reducing. Both benches sustain the timing objection - $1.59, only 12.8% off the $1.41 low, no confirmed catalyst within 90 days, next print ~2026-11-09 and UNCONFIRMED - which under the response taxonomy is a tranche/wait objection, not a kill. Blue's disposition is that demand is confirmed intact (+13% GWh), funding adequacy remains a computable open question, and the name stays on the docket at roughly 5/10 with named re-entry gates. That is a materially different instruction to the conveyor than red's 'kill the docket', and it is not mine to settle. || SESSION RULING: ESCALATION RULED: docket RETAINED (blue's branch) — red's kill was wrong on 2 of 3 FATALs (Up-C exchange artifact misread as 2x dilution; $562M undrawn facilities omitted). Do not ratify a kill whose prosecution failed arithmetic audit. FLAT at tape stands (both benches agree); WATCH with blue's reopen gates.
